questions.q: Which three Apex classes are used together to make an HTTP callout?
options: RestRequest, RestResponse, RestContext
Http, HttpRequest, HttpResponse
Database, DmlException, SaveResult
EventBus, ChangeEventHeader, Database.SaveResult
questions.explain: HttpRequest builds the outgoing request, Http.send() performs the callout, and HttpResponse holds the result.

options: A strongly-typed Apex SObject matching the response
A generic Object, typically cast to Map<String, Object> or List<Object>, representing the parsed JSON
The raw, unparsed JSON string
An HttpResponse object
questions.explain: deserializeUntyped() parses JSON into generic Apex collections (Maps and Lists) you navigate with casts, as opposed to deserialize() into a specific wrapper class.

questions.q: What happens if HttpRequest.setMethod() is never called before sending the request?
options: The request defaults to GET automatically
It throws a runtime error, since no method was set
The request defaults to POST automatically
Salesforce infers the method from whether a body was set
questions.explain: An HttpRequest has no default method — omitting setMethod() throws a runtime error, so it must always be set explicitly.

questions.q: A callout completes with no exception thrown, but the remote API actually returned a 500 error in the response body. What mistake does this scenario illustrate?
options: Treating "no exception was thrown" as proof the callout succeeded, instead of checking getStatusCode()
Forgetting to call JSON.serialize() on the request
Using a Named Credential instead of a literal URL
Setting Content-Type to application/json
questions.explain: A callout can complete without a CalloutException while the remote system still reports failure via its HTTP status code — the status code must be checked explicitly.

questions.q: Why should real integration code use `callout:My_Named_Credential/...` as the endpoint rather than a literal URL with an inline API key?
options: Literal URLs are not supported by the Http class at all
A Named Credential keeps the endpoint and authentication secret out of the Apex code and debug logs, resolved only at send time
Literal URLs always time out after 1 second
Named Credentials are required for every SOAP callout but optional for HTTP callouts
questions.explain: Hard-coding a URL and secret defeats the security separation Named Credentials provide, exposing the secret in code and logs instead of resolving it only at send time.
